articles.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
articles.description: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
articles.summary: An analysis of 2,884 exploding stars provides new evidence about dark energy and its role in the Universe's expansion, offering insights into one of cosmology's greatest mysteries.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover just shattered the all-time off-world driving record
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has shattered a historic space exploration record, traveling farther across another world than any vehicle before it. Its advanced self-driving system helped it surpass Opportunity’s 28.06-mile record in just five and a half years, a feat that previously took nearly 15. Now, Perseverance is exploring some of the oldest rocks in the solar system, searching for clues about ancient Martian environments that may once have supported life.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has set a new off-world driving record, traveling farther across Mars than any rover in history.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
articles.description: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago.
articles.summary: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe's earliest moments by measuring key properties from the first five minutes after the Big Bang.

articles.title: IceCube, high-energy neutrinos, and Francis Halzen win 2026’s Physics Nobel
articles.description:
Back in 1988, Francis Halzen had what he called a “cute idea.” His vision grew into the IceCube observatory, and earns the 2026 Nobel…
Continue reading on Starts With A Bang! »
articles.summary: Francis Halzen and the IceCube observatory win the 2026 Physics Nobel Prize for detecting high-energy neutrinos from space, opening a revolutionary new window into the cosmos.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Charts Path for Roman with Gravitational Lenses
articles.description: This observation is one of many gravitational lensing images taken by Hubble in preparation for science with the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.summary: Hubble's gravitational lensing observations are paving the way for groundbreaking science with NASA's upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The First […]
articles.summary: APOD highlights the first-ever discovered green star, WD J1330+6435, a remarkable and unusual stellar object that challenges astronomical understanding.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully launches toward Mars's intriguing moon Phobos for groundbreaking scientific study.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates a major milestone as the ESA-JAXA Mercury exploration mission completes eight years of remarkable scientific achievements.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope makes its first discovery of a previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's exceptional observational capabilities.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The ESA-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft traces the mysterious magnetic switchbacks in solar wind, advancing our understanding of dynamic solar phenomena.

articles.title: JWST Reveals a Lopsided Alien World with Blistering Evening Winds
articles.description: Typically, when we think of exoplanets, we think of neat spheres floating directly in front of their star, which acts as a giant spotlight. From our vantage point, they would look more like two perfect two dimensional circles than spheres, though. But nature is almost never so clean-cut. A new paper published in Nature Astronomy from researchers at Cornell and the University of Bristol details the first-ever study of an exoplanet that is noticeably lopsided.
articles.summary: JWST has revealed an asymmetrical exoplanet with extreme wind patterns on its evening side, challenging our understanding of planetary atmospheres. This discovery demonstrates the telescope's ability to reveal exotic worlds beyond our solar system.

articles.title: Even the Rubin's Test Camera Produces Stunning Images
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory's Commissioning Camera operated for about 7 weeks in 2024, before the observatory released its well-known first look images. It's an engineering camera, and its job was to test the VRO's equipment and procedures. Now, the VRO has released the ComCam's image of the Seagull nebula. It's a pretty stunning image for an engineering camera.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory's commissioning camera produced exceptional images during its 7-week test run in 2024. These results demonstrate the observatory's potential for revolutionary astronomical discoveries.

articles.title: Two Disks in One: How Accretion Disks Drive Black Hole Jets
articles.description: SMBH jets are driven by thick, hot accretion disks with powerful magnetic fields. But there's a bit of a paradox. Some SMBH produce jets, even though they appear to have thin, cold accretion disks. New research has solved this paradox, showing that disks can be truncated into an outer cold disk and an inner hot disk.
articles.summary: New research reveals how thick, hot accretion disks with powerful magnetic fields drive supermassive black hole jets. This discovery resolves a key paradox in black hole physics.

articles.title: New Evidence for an Old Prediction: Recoiling Supermassive Black Holes
articles.description: Theory says that during some SMBH mergers, the merger remnant receives a recoil kick from gravitational waves. Instead of sitting placidly in the galactic center, these recoiled SMBH are sent on a pendulum-like motion, back and forth through the galactic center. New research has found statistical evidence supporting their existence.
articles.summary: Researchers have found new evidence supporting the prediction that supermassive black holes experience recoil kicks from gravitational waves during mergers. This validates decades-old theoretical predictions.

articles.title: Autonomous Triangular Modules Could Build Tomorrow’s Mega-Observatories
articles.description: Private companies are getting better and better at launching more and more mass into space with larger and larger rockets. But, there is still a major constraint on the size of objects we can get into orbit - fairing size. This places physical constraints on the overall shape of what we can launch, and severely limits the sizes of, say, a communications array or a power satellite. But a new paper from researchers at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and the Beijing Institute of Technology offers a solution - a self-shaping, deployable module that can fine-tune both its positioning and its own dimensions.
articles.summary: Autonomous triangular modules could revolutionize the construction of massive space observatories in orbit. This innovation leverages advances in rocket technology to enable ambitious astronomical facilities.

articles.title: Supernova Explosions First Aided, Then Later Impeded, the Epoch of Reionization
articles.description: The Epoch of Reionization is when radiation from early galaxies and their stars reionized neutral hydrogen and let light travel freely through the cosmos. Some research shows that supernovae helped the process. But new research shows that, though they may have helped initially, supernovae eventually slowed reionization.
articles.summary: Research shows how supernova explosions both aided and later impeded the Epoch of Reionization in the early universe. This complex relationship reveals new insights into cosmic evolution and star formation history.

articles.title: Autonomous triangular modules could build tomorrow's mega-observatories
articles.description: Private companies are getting better at launching more mass into space with larger rockets. But there is still a major constraint on the size of objects we can get into orbit—fairing size. This places physical constraints on the overall shape of what we can launch and severely limits the sizes of, say, a communications array or a power satellite. But a new paper from researchers at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and the Beijing Institute of Technology offers a solution—a self-shaping, deployable module that can fine-tune both its positioning and its own dimensions. The findings are published in the journal Space: Science & Technology.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Autonomous triangular modules represent a breakthrough approach to building massive space observatories using advanced rocket launch capabilities. This technology enables the construction of next-generation astronomical facilities.

articles.title: Webb captures stars in the early stages of life in a nearby stellar nursery
articles.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope continues to reveal hidden parts of the cosmos with its advanced suite of infrared instruments. In a newly released image, Webb revealed many stars previously hidden by the dust clouds of NGC 7129, a stellar nursery about 3,300 light-years from Earth in the constellation Cepheus. The image is already improving our understanding of how new stars are born and evolve with time.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: JWST has captured stunning images of young stars in their early formation stages within a nearby stellar nursery. These observations reveal the hidden processes of star birth in unprecedented detail.

articles.title: Webb image reveals young stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description: In this Picture of the Month from the NASA/ESA James Webb Space Telescope, we visit a turbulent cauldron of star formation to see what is brewing inside dense clumps of gas. This is a star-forming region named LHA 120-N 159, or simply N159, located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This image spans about 230 light-years across.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Webb has imaged a dynamic stellar nursery revealing young stars being born in a turbulent nebular environment. This Picture of the Month showcases the telescope's ability to peer into star-forming regions.

articles.title: Supermassive black holes ejected from galactic centers? Quasar survey supports decade-old prediction
articles.description: By analyzing data on around 100,000 quasars, or extremely luminous galactic nuclei, researchers at Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) have found statistical evidence that some supermassive black holes at the centers of galaxies are ejected from their positions after forming. The relationship now identified in the data was predicted 10 years ago by members of the same research group, Peter Raffai and Zsolt Frei, together with Zoltán Haiman.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A quasar survey of ~100,000 objects supports the theoretical prediction that supermassive black holes can be ejected from galactic centers. This discovery validates decade-old theoretical models of black hole dynamics.

articles.title: Black hole observations uncover evidence of solar storm–like magnetic eruptions
articles.description: Technion researchers have presented evidence for the existence of solar-storm-like outbursts near supermassive black holes, which can be a million times larger than the sun or more. The phenomenon was discovered in the vicinity of the black hole in the galaxy NGC 3783, and the researchers' findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Technion researchers have discovered evidence of solar-storm-like magnetic eruptions occurring near supermassive black holes, revealing dynamic processes similar to those on our Sun.

articles.title: NASA’s Curiosity rover reveals a spectacular new view of Mars with a mystery on the horizon
articles.description: NASA’s Curiosity rover has revealed a spectacular new view of mysterious, wind-carved cliffs on Mars that may hold evidence of ancient volcanic activity. With the rover approaching these unusual formations, scientists hope to uncover the secrets behind their strange appearance in 2027.
articles.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover has captured spectacular imagery of wind-carved cliffs on Mars that may contain evidence of past geological activity and water presence.

articles.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
articles.description: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight. Researchers found that astronauts' hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and handled simulated Martian gravity without major problems, offering new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.
articles.summary: A study of 13 astronauts reveals that the human heart is surprisingly well-adapted for long-duration space travel, offering encouraging insights for future Mars missions.

articles.title: NASA solves a strange mystery hidden inside asteroid Bennu’s boulders
articles.description: NASA scientists have finally uncovered why asteroid Bennu loses heat so quickly despite being covered in massive boulders. Samples returned to Earth reveal that its rocks are filled with hidden cracks, solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years.
articles.summary: NASA scientists have solved a mystery about asteroid Bennu's rapid heat loss, uncovering new insights into the thermal properties of asteroid surfaces.

articles.title: NASA reveals 16 stunning galaxies hiding cosmic chaos
articles.description: NASA's stunning new gallery of 16 galaxies reveals colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular cosmic collisions through the combined power of Chandra, James Webb, Hubble, and other telescopes. These extraordinary images expose the hidden forces shaping galaxies across the universe and offer clues about the Milky Way's own past and future.
articles.summary: NASA's gallery of 16 stunning galaxies reveals spectacular cosmic phenomena including black hole jets and explosive star formation across the Universe.

articles.title: Private Griffin moon lander gets put to the test | Space photo of the day for Oct. 23, 2026
articles.description: The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year.
articles.summary: The Griffin lunar lander has successfully passed critical tests in preparation for its first crewed moon landing mission.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the…
articles.summary: NASA JPL envisions the next 90 years of space exploration with ambitious innovations including interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Martian helicopters, pushing the boundaries of human discovery.

articles.title: A Quantum Cyclotron for Antimatter
articles.description: Author(s): Paolo CrivelliA device that stores a single positron and controls its quantum states could measure its magnetic moment with unprecedented precision, testing a symmetry principle central to quantum field theory.[Physics 19, 132] Published Wed Oct 21…
articles.summary: A quantum cyclotron device can store and control a single positron's quantum states, enabling precise measurements of antimatter properties and advancing fundamental physics research.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Astronomers have confirmed the first microblazar, a cosmic object with properties distinct from extragalactic blazars, expanding our understanding of high-energy astrophysical phenomena.

articles.title: Astronomers Uncover More Intriguing Detail in an Ancient Supernova Remnant
articles.description: When a supernova exploded in 1181, Chinese and Japanese sky-watchers recorded it. They couldn't have known what the object was, and why it appeared for six months then disappeared. But in our modern times, we know it was a supernova, and we've even, most like…
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered new intriguing details in a 1181 supernova remnant recorded by ancient Chinese and Japanese observers, deepening our understanding of stellar explosions and historical astronomical records.
